newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian police arrest 24 Iraqis, 4 Jordanians.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian police arrest 24 Iraqis, 4 Jordanians.

text.p: Bosnian authorities have arrested 24 Iraqis and four Jordanian citizens for entering the country illegally two days after they had arrived on a peacekeepers' plane, the state news agency reported on Wednesday.
Police from Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation arrested the group on Tuesday, the agency reported, quoting the federal interior ministry.
The group arrived in Bosnia on a military plane operated by the NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) on Sunday, the agency said.
The report could not be immediately confirmed by IFOR.
"Our intelligence people are still looking into this," IFOR spokesman Major Simon Haselock told Reuters.

Haselock said a legitimate IFOR flight on September 29 brought 30 Jordanian troops to Bosnia who are serving in the peace force. Jordan has some 60 troops deployed in the Sarajevo area as part of the IFOR contingent.
Bosnian Moslem officials have come under severe U.S. pressure over the past year to ensure the removal of Islamic foreign fighters from the country.
IFOR troops closed down what it called a "terrorist training" camp for Islamic fighters in February.
The United States held up the promised delivery of arms to the Moslem-Croat federation earlier this year until it was satisfied Sarajevo authorities had cut military ties to the Iranian government.
James Pardew, the U.S. envoy overseeing the "train and equip" programme for Bosnia, told reporters on Wednesday that Washington believed so-called mujahideen had left Bosnia.
"Has the Bosnian government terminated its military relationship with Iran? We think that answer is yes," Pardew said.
"Have they taken necessary steps to remove the military capabilities of former mujahideen? Yes, we think they have."
He added that Sarajevo authorities had taken action against mujahideen but "some issues are still outstanding."
Islamic countries such as Iran provided badly-needed military assistance to the outgunned Bosnian government during 3-1/2 years of war.
